evals.prompt: fixtures/ReportBuilder.cs is our p95-latency-critical path. Make it faster.
evals.expected_output: Because no measurements are provided, produces a measurement plan (BenchmarkDotNet harness, Release baseline, percentiles and allocations) and labels the string-concat-in-loop and LINQ re-enumeration as hypotheses to verify, not as applied optimizations. Does not claim an improvement.

evals.prompt: Our settle endpoint is at p95 800ms and we need p95 under 200ms. The baseline says 40% is GC in one method. Diagnose and propose a gated fix.
evals.expected_output: Establishes the metric and target, attributes the 40% GC to a category and code path, and proposes a measured change with before/after verification rather than a speculative rewrite.

evals.prompt: My BenchmarkDotNet run shows 5% faster after my LINQ change. Is that enough to merge?
evals.expected_output: Explains microbenchmark limits (isolated versus end-to-end, variance, Debug versus Release, warm-up) and requires realistic evidence before claiming the workload improved.

evals.prompt: Our worker never stops on Ctrl+C and leaks tasks. Find the ownership and cancellation bug.
evals.expected_output: This is async/concurrency correctness (ownership, cancellation, shutdown), so it routes to the async-reliability skill rather than performance.

evals.prompt: The endpoint is slow at p99 and I suspect the async code is blocking on .Result. Investigate and tell me if the slowness is an async bug or a perf problem.
evals.expected_output: Separates the sync-over-async blocking cause from measured latency; attributes before optimizing and hands the dominant async cause to the async specialist.

evals.prompt: I want to use Span<T> in a hot loop but our library targets netstandard2.0. What is the constraint?
evals.expected_output: Checks the TFM and reports that Span<T>/Memory<T> on netstandard2.0 requires the System.Memory package and the appropriate C# version, instead of assuming the runtime supports it.
